chapter: Chicago: Henderson, Tatum and Roy Eldridge, then New York and the army
title: Using the army years to practice
summary: In the army he practiced and compared what he heard on New York trips, returning in 1946 to a changed bebop scene.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: But normally I had a chance to really kind of get it together, to formulate all the things, you know, that I had been -- because it was like, being on the inside looking out or outside looking in. I don't know, I could see what they were doing, but there I could get away from it. I was almost like an observer, you know. I would go to New York and I would see what everybody was doing, and I had a chance to compare, and I would go back and I would just work, and work. So actually it wasn't a total loss.
But when I came out, the whole scene had changed now. I mean, music had changed, styles had changed, bebop was the thing, and so I had this woodshed again, you see.
